messages:
jordan: Heads up — canary run for engine-kernel v3.2.1-rc + q8_2 quant on A100s has been flapping for ~4h. Throughput drops intermittently in matmul microbench on us-west-2 canary pool. Seen on 3 separate hosts.

jordan: quick snippet from bench logs:```
bench: step 142: tokens/s=1200 -> 950 (p50->p90 shift)
device: a100-80gb
config: q8_2 + matmul-v2
stack: matmul_v2_fp16_accel -> scheduler
```

maya: ugh, that sounds like the staging matmul regression we flagged last week. Any thermal triggers?

anil: +1 — need to rule out thermal or power gating first. Which host IDs?

jordan: host ids: canary01, canary03, canary07. Temps look normal (~66-70C). Not pure thermal. Correlates to kernel path matmul_v2_fp16_accel. perfbot attached microbench run.

perfbot: microbench report (canary01): p95 latency +28% at 2026-03-20T02:14Z. Regression cluster narrowed to kernel-scheduler path after rc6..rc11 builds.

jen: recommendation: hold the night cutover. Pin canary group to engine:3.1.9 until we triage.

jordan: agree. Would prefer a sticky pin for canaries only so we don't block internal test clusters.

deploy-bot: @jen requested: apply sticky pin on canary-group -> engine:3.1.9. Command to ops: `/deploy pin canary-group engine:3.1.9 --sticky-ttl 6h`
deploy-bot: Pin applied ✅ (canary-group -> engine:3.1.9) by jen at 2026-03-20T03:05Z

maya: can we instead do a partial traffic shift: keep 95% pinned, 5% on rc11 with extra telemetry? Safer for bisecting in production.

anil: I'm leaning toward full pin for all canaries until we bisect. Sean, can you run a quick bisect between rc6..rc11?

sean: on it. Triggering bisect job: `/ci bisect --range rc6..rc11 --bench matmul_micro --targets=canary01,canary03`

jordan: I'll update the release notes draft. Add a KNOWN_ISSUE block: "intermittent matmul microbench throughput drop on some A100 hosts; mitigation: canary pin to 3.1.9; investigating root cause."

jen: also add an ops-runbook entry: auto-fallback to 3.1.9 if error-rate > 0.5% or tokens/s degradation > 10% for 15m. Notify support and customers if we unpin later.

support-runbook: Created ticket RW-4573 and webhook to ops. Playbook stub at /runbooks/matmul-flap.md

sean: bisect result: culprit traced to commit 7f2d3a5 — matmul kernel reorder in matmul_v2.cc. Reproduces locally when forcing single-stream scheduling.

jordan: great catch. Proposed plan: revert 7f2d3a5 in rc-squash branch, run a quick qbuild (fast profile), smoke on pinned canary group. If green, prepare a rolling night cutover with 15% initial slice and the p95 + tokens/s gates.

anil: add smoke gate criteria here: p95 <= 1.2x baseline AND tokens/s degradation < 5% across canary pool for 30m. If fail, auto-roll back to 3.1.9.

jen: noted. I'll update release notes and coordinate changelog. Also will set deploy-bot sticky-ttl to extend if we need more time.

maya: timeline: if revert + qbuild + smoke completes within ~2h we can consider reintroducing a patched rc to 10% overnight. Otherwise keep canaries on 3.1.9 until morning.

sean: started the revert PR and kicked off quick qbuild: `/ci build --profile quick rc-squash-revert-7f2d3a5`

perfbot: quick smoke on canary-group (3.1.9 pinned) shows baseline metrics stable for 45m. p95 and tokens/s within thresholds.

jordan: checklist before we allow unpinning: [1] merged revert + green qbuild smoke, [2] bisect confirmed, [3] telemetry stable for 60m after unpin test, [4] release notes updated + customer notice draft.

maya: ok, will stand by for green. Thanks team :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: NOTE: canary-group remains pinned to engine:3.1.9. To unpin after validation use `/deploy unpin canary-group` (ops approval required).

jen: I'll send an ops p2 note if anything regresses. If all green, I'll coordinate the 15% night slice and post to #customer-notify before unpin.

jordan: thanks everyone — closing for now, reopen if new regression pops up.
